Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — A solid autumn soaring day with deep, sharp thermals and no cloud overdevelopment. Winds are generally light to moderate but direction varies considerably across the region, making some sites off-angle at times. Best opportunities are at the thermal sites mid-day, though strong lapse rates demand advanced pilot skills.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Marginal — wind is cross to tail (268–287°) for the SE-facing preferred direction all day, with strong early gusts to 23 mph. Flying window 10am–3pm, peak w* 279 ft/min, thermal ceiling 2278 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 8.9 °C/km).
  • Hallelujah: Favorable — wind shifts on-slot (W/SW) from 2pm onward, though thermal production is strong earlier. Flying window 11am–6pm, peak w* 416 ft/min, thermal ceiling 6154 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 10.0 °C/km — advanced only). Good evening soaring potential after 6pm with drainage winds NW/N.
  • Slide Mountain: Marginal — wind is off-angle (W/NW) for the S/SE launch early, becoming more aligned late but thermals shut down by 4pm. Peak layer speed shear of 6 mph flagged. Flying window 9am–3pm, peak w* 351 ft/min, thermal ceiling 3749 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 8.6 °C/km).
  • McClellan: Favorable — light and variable early, wind shifts on-slot (W/SW) 3–6pm, with a strong thermal prime window. Flying window 11am–5pm, peak w* 461 ft/min, thermal ceiling 4956 ft AGL. Peak layer speed shear of 6 mph flagged. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.6 °C/km — advanced only).
  • West McClellan: Marginal — wind direction is S/SW all day, over 30° off the preferred W/NW direction; peak layer direction change of 31° flagged. Flying window 11am–4pm, peak w* 380 ft/min, thermal ceiling 3834 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.1 °C/km).
  • Peavine Mountain: Favorable — wind is consistently SW/W throughout the day, well within preferred arc; moderate speeds. Flying window 10am–4pm, peak w* 376 ft/min, thermal ceiling 5076 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.6 °C/km — advanced only).
  • Rainbow Ridge: Favorable — wind becomes on-slot (W/NW) from 1pm onward and remains steady through evening; strong thermal production. Flying window 10am–6pm, peak w* 426 ft/min, thermal ceiling 5897 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.9 °C/km — advanced only).
  • Duck Hill: Marginal — wind is SE early, then shifts on-slot (W/NW) from 3pm; peak layer speed shear of 7 mph flagged. Flying window 11am–6pm, peak w* 417 ft/min, thermal ceiling 5672 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.8 °C/km — advanced only). Evening soaring possible after 6pm.
  • Daydreams: Unfavorable — very weak thermal production (peak w* only 90 ft/min) with on-slot wind arriving after thermals die. No meaningful flying window today.

Hazards

  • Sharp thermals: All sites except Daydreams show lapse rates of 8.6–10.0 °C/km, indicating strong, punchy thermals suitable only for advanced/expert pilots.
  • Low-level speed shear: Slide Mountain (6 mph/layer), McClellan (6 mph/layer), West McClellan (5 mph/layer), and Duck Hill (7 mph/layer) exceed 5 mph/layer threshold — risk of shear turbulence on approach and landing.
  • Low-level directional shear: West McClellan peaks at 31° layer change, near the 30° threshold for shear hazard.
  • Bulk shear: McClellan (22 mph) and Duck Hill (22 mph) show significant 10m→500m AGL shear, potentially linked to approaching wind shift or thermal-gradient effects.
  • Rotor/lee turbulence: Persistent westerly component aloft may generate lee-side rotor downwind of Peavine Mountain and the Carson Range; caution in mid-afternoon when thermal mixing activates these zones.
